newsitem.title: czech republic: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 16.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - With the help of votes from two representatives of the Social Democratic Party (CSSD), parliament approved the government budget for 1997.

- From February of next year, all transactions (including their prices), which appear on the capital market and go through the Security Centre (SCP), will be publicised. Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced this yesterday in a meeting aimed at analysing the market situation and finding possibilities for improvement.

- An increase in value added tax (DPH) tariffs from the current five percent to 22 percent could have a very negative impact on housing construction, according to the president of the Union of Construction Contractors, Milan Veverka.

- The possibility of financial aid from the United States to the value of 240 million dollars for Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic for buying military technology is apparently not existent. Czech Defence Minister, Miloslav Vyborny, and defence ministers from the other two countries were sceptical about the offer from the start.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - The employees of Poldi Steel Works, who will not receive their normal Christmas bonuses this year, are blaming it on the arrest of the majority owner, Vladimir Stehlik.

PRAVO - Jozef Wagner and Tomas Teplik, whose votes caused the approval of the government budget, were expelled by their party - the Social Democrats (CSSD). CSSD has been against approval of the budget since the beginning.
